reasoning: Skeptic lane. Q4 FY26 (Nov 19) was a clean beat: revenue $1,994M vs $1.94B guide midpoint and $1.95B consensus, orders $2,339M (book-to-bill 1.17), Q1 guide $2.05B vs $1.96B consensus, FY27 base case +20% (src 1, 2, 12). Keysight has beaten all seven first quarterly guides I could score (median +2.8%). The downside case therefore does not rest on near-term execution but on the cycle: (1) growth is concentrated in AI wireline (comms ~84% of Q4 y/y growth, src 27), which is a test build tied to hyperscaler capex whose 2026 growth is partly memory-price inflation (src 18); (2) the FY26 growth included 7 points of acquisitions and ~110bp of one-time tariff-refund gross margin (src 2); (3) Keysight's own history shows a 42.6% drawdown in 2021-23 and a 39% operating-income fall in FY24 while the business kept growing in parts (src 22, F1, F2); (4) the stock reversed post-earnings gains in August and again on Nov 20 with the AI-hardware tape (src 26, 30). Things I checked that are not red flags: credit (Baa1, net cash $407M, src 24, 1), insider selling (~$4.9M over 180 days, small, ~31% under 10b5-1, src 23), GAAP vs non-GAAP gap ($513M, mostly acquisition amortization and integration, src 27). Model: three end-market segments driven by J.P. Morgan Big-5 capex (+42% 2027, then my +15%/+10%) at a fitted 0.55 elasticity, a defense index (+8/+6/+5%) and SEMI 300mm equipment (to $227B in 2029) at a 0.64 elasticity; CSG/EISG margins peak at 35%/31% in FY27 and revert toward the long-term target by FY29. FY27 revenue $8.29B (+15.9%) sits 3.4% below management's base case and 1.7% above pre-print consensus; FY27 non-GAAP EPS ~$14.2 is 3% above consensus $13.77. Exit P/E 19.5x (own 19.0x shrunk toward the 21.45x peer median) and FCF yield 3.82% give $293.7 and $308.9; research target (12m) $299.8, +14.6% vs the Nov 20 close. Downside P10 $163 (flat FY27 revenue, ~28% margins, 14.5x) is a genuine 1-in-10 given 48% realized vol; upside P90 $422. Research was limited by blocked sec.gov filing text (XBRL used instead) and by the Nasdaq/Zacks consensus page carrying no date, so I used the dated Nov 19 consensus quoted by stock3.

model_inputs.structure_note: Driver-led annual set (3 end-market segments, 100% of revenue driven): commercial comms = hyperscaler capex ^ elasticity, ADG = defense spending index, EI = 300mm fab equipment ^ elasticity; CSG/EISG margins as drivers with FY29 a mid-cycle year. Value carried by P/E (0.6) and FCF yield (0.4, the tech FCF-leg rule) on the build's own NTM/LTM figures; no DCF, no SOTP (all segments sell to the same electronics R&D/production capex cycle).
model_inputs.gap_note: 1) Annual, not quarterly: QBRIEF asks driver models for quarters; this agent set is annual for time, so quarter EPS tie-out (rule 29) is not built; net non-operating cost ~$25M/yr pre-tax (~$0.12/share, ~0.8% of EPS) is left out with interest_rate 0. 2) FCF yield leg uses engine FCFF after SBC (ebit_basis adjusted, sbc cost), more conservative than the no-SBC-deduction rule by ~$1.4/share of FCF (~10% on that leg, ~4% on the target): a judgment for Kilian. 3) Only 4 whole-company peers (VIAV, TER, AME, FTV); FORM, ONTO, KLAC, CDNS are segment-only (<25% of revenue each). 4) No financing event: net cash, $833M authorization, Baa1 (src 24), probability of an equity or debt raise <5%; a large acquisition (Keysight bought Spirent, OSG, PowerArtist in FY25 for ~$2.0B) is ~25% likely over 12 months but is value-neutral at the price paid, so not modeled. 5) Judgment calls sized with the engine: CSG margin held at the Q4 exit +5.8% and reverted to the 31.5% target -7.5%; comm elasticity at the FY25 fit -8.2%; FCF-yield own basis July TTM +5.9%: these four move the research target (12m) more than 5% and go to Kilian. Capex path alternatives (Dell'Oro +2.8%, Moody's -3.1%, flat CY28 -2.6%), defense (+1.0%) and EI elasticity (+1.1%) do not.
